name: Winterthur Museum
unique: Henry du Pont's 175-room mansion holding the world's premier collection of American decorative arts, set in 60 acres of naturalistic garden.
buzz: The period rooms are jaw-dropping; the garden tram is the sleeper hit. Some find the guided only format slow.

name: Fort Delaware
unique: A moat ringed Civil War fortress on an island in the Delaware River, reached by ferry, with prison barracks, tunnels and a living history garrison.
buzz: The ferry and the moat make it an adventure; the prison history is grim and well told. Bring lunch, there is nothing on the island.

name: Dogfish Head Brewery Tour
unique: The brewery that invented continual hopping and put American craft beer on the map, with a tour that includes the original 1995 brewhouse and a tasting.
buzz: Tours are praised for honesty about failures and for generous pours; book ahead and eat at the brewpub.

name: Nemours Estate
unique: A 77-room French neoclassical mansion built by Alfred du Pont, with formal gardens modeled on Versailles and a garage full of vintage cars.
buzz: Less crowded than the du Pont mansions in Pennsylvania; reviews praise the gardens and the car collection.

name: Cape Henlopen and Fort Miles
unique: A WWII coastal defense fort with a concrete observation tower you can climb, plus dunes, bay beach and ocean beach in one park.
buzz: The tower tour is the reason to come; the beaches are quieter than Rehoboth. Bikes are the best way around.

name: Rehoboth Beach Boardwalk
unique: A mile of boardwalk with a 1920s merry-go-round, Thrasher's fries in vinegar and a beach town that still shuts its bars early.
buzz: It is the Mid-Atlantic's cleanest family beach; parking is the eternal complaint. Go in September.
